paragraphs: Rav Hanina of Sura on the Euphrates.

[Bava Metzia 61b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.61b.8) relates that Ravina visited Sura on the Euphrates; Hyman cites [Rashi's explanation](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Bava_Metzia.61b.8.1) that this is not ordinary Sura. Rav Chanina of Sura on the Euphrates asks Ravina why the Exodus is mentioned in the law of creeping creatures, etc. [Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1471&lang=en) conjectures Rav Chaviva of Sura on the Euphrates. Hyman comments, “A sage is preferable to a prophet,” reporting that this reading occurs in the source supplied as ברק״ם and in [Sheiltot, Vaera](https://www.sefaria.org/Sheiltot_d'Rav_Achai_Gaon.43.1).[^1][^2][^3]

notes.text: The supporting-source siglum ברק״ם remains unresolved. Hyman’s sage-better-than-prophet comment celebrates the apparent confirmation of Seder HaDorot’s conjecture; it is not a new identification made here.
The linked Bavli has Rav Chanina ask Ravina about the Exodus in the law of creeping creatures. The linked Rashi distinguishes Sura on the Euphrates from ordinary Sura.

Hyman’s print (vol. II, p. 499) gives Chanina and discusses the proposed Chaviva reading. The linked Heilprin entry suggests that Chanina may be the Chaviva elsewhere, while the linked Sheiltot explicitly names Rav Chaviva in this same exchange. The siglum ברק״ם is unresolved.
